Root issue to address: current gameplay resolves routed_lane = (source_lane + rotor_step) % 6, while the central visual is a simple rotating straight conduit. The player cannot reliably infer from the picture where an incoming pulse will exit. Fix the visual/mechanic seam so the result of each A/D rotation is immediately understandable without mental arithmetic.

1) Create a single authoritative route-mapping helper used by BOTH gameplay resolution and any route-preview/onboarding visualization. Do not duplicate routing math in separate systems.

The preview must update immediately when A/D or arrow input rotates the core.
3) Clearly distinguish the pulse's TARGET destination from the CURRENT routed destination using the existing symbol-first accessibility design. Highlight the matching target glyph/terminal and show an unmistakable success-ready indication when current route == target; show a clearly different not-yet-aligned state otherwise. Color may assist but must not be the only signal.
4) Add a short learn-by-doing onboarding for the first few pulses (for example 2-3 assisted pulses) that demonstrates: incoming pulse -> target symbol -> rotate -> route aligned -> success. It must not rely on paragraph instructions alone. Slow or otherwise safely stage the assisted pulses if needed so a first-time player has time to react. After onboarding, normal 90-second score-attack behavior should take over.
5) Improve feedback at resolution so a correct route and a misroute are visually unmistakable. Preserve score, multiplier, three-overload rule, deterministic seed semantics, SDK lifecycle, RunTicket strictness, exact-origin/source checks, visibility pause, export policy, and portal integration unless a very narrow change is required by this correction.
6) Update the portal briefing/control copy to plain language that matches the actual mechanic. Avoid jargon such as "radial glyph conduits" as the primary explanation.
7) Add deterministic behavioral tests for the shared route-mapping helper and onboarding state transitions. At minimum prove all six source lanes × six rotor steps map consistently, preview/result cannot disagree, and assisted onboarding exits into normal play. Do not replace behavioral tests with source substring checks.
8) Preserve all previously passing strict timestamp, web-bridge typing, ticket, daily-seed, host lifecycle, and export tests.
